_comment: Baseline for the RDD2 simulation hot-loop performance guard (ledger #32).
Consumed by crates/rumoca/tests/rdd2_perf_guard.rs, which also reads
`source_root` on behalf of crates/rumoca/tests/galec_review_surface.rs so
both RDD2 gates agree on which checkout they measure.
THE REPORTED STATISTIC IS A MINIMUM, NOT A MEAN, AND IT IS ONLY ASSERTED
ON A QUIET MACHINE. Two designs were tried and measured before this one:
* single run + mean + 25% tolerance: failed 3/3 under 32-core saturation
(+77.1%, +73.7%, +68.8%) with no regression present;
* minimum of 3 invocations: still failed under the same saturation
(+67.3%, +67.6%). Saturation raises the floor on this workload -- it
competes for memory bandwidth, not just for a timeslice -- so every
sample inflates and the minimum inflates with them.
The gate therefore measures how busy the machine was over its own sampling
window (from /proc/stat) and asserts only below `max_cpu_busy_fraction`.
Above it, every number is still printed but nothing is asserted.
`max_cpu_busy_fraction` is the measured knee, which is sharp and sits close
to fully saturated. Inflation of the gated statistic against machine load:
busy 0.098 -> baseline    busy 0.751 -> - 7.4%  (enforced, passed)
busy 0.667 -> +10.6%      busy 0.997 -> +59.7%  (not enforced)
busy 0.999 -> +68.4%  (not enforced)
Everything below ~0.92 stays well inside the 25% tolerance -- at 0.751 there
was no inflation at all. An earlier revision guessed 0.25 to be safe, which
was worse than useless: the gate's own bench load puts roughly 11 points of
busy into its own measurement window, so at 0.25 it enforced in 0 of 8 trials
on a normal box even with a 10x regression injected. 0.85 keeps every
enforcing condition inside the tolerance while letting the gate actually
fire.
HOW TO REGENERATE (a recorded decision -- see the ratchet note below):
1. Build the RELEASE binary; the baseline is a release-profile number and
a debug binary is roughly an order of magnitude slower:
cargo build --release -p rumoca
2. Run the canonical bench on an otherwise idle machine:
./target/release/rumoca sim bench \
<source_root>/Vehicles/package.mo \
--model Vehicles.Rdd2.Test.WaypointMission \
--source-root <source_root> \
--t-end 0.5 --dt 0.005 --solver rk-like \
--iterations 5 --warmups 2 --json
3. Repeat step 2 at least `invocations` times and copy the SMALLEST
`hot_best_seconds` into `hot_best_seconds` below, with the date and the
machine it came from. Use the minimum, not the median: the baseline and
the gate must be the same statistic or the tolerance means nothing.
`source_root` is the checkout of the (out-of-tree) modelica_models library.
Resolution order is MODELICAPATH, then this value. A missing corpus is a
HARD FAILURE with instructions, not a skip: these gates only compile when
their feature is explicitly requested, so a silent pass would mean nothing
was measured. The value below is this developer's path, kept as a
documented default rather than baked into the Rust source.
`corpus_revision` is the modelica_models commit every number here and every
ceiling in galec_review_surface.rs was measured against. Both gates print
the corpus commit they actually saw and flag a mismatch, so a ratchet
failure can be attributed to the compiler or to the corpus rather than
being ambiguous.
recorded_notes: Measured with the release binary built from galec-c-integration (55ea493c) merged with the GALEC C working-memory overlay (8b4a9840). Three invocations gave hot_best_seconds 0.1723 / 0.1617 / 0.1613; the gated minimum is 0.1613. Validated under deliberate 32-core saturation -- see the guard's module docs.
